transcript: Last night, Paul and I went to Titanic at New York City Center, the final show this year's Encores series. This is a simply staged production highlighting the lush score beautifully performed by an all-star cast and a fantastically full orchestra. I went into this pretty blind, having never seen the unrelated but very famous Titanic movie, but obviously knowing how it would end. And I gotta say, it's kind of a strange show — there's not really a specific main character, we just see scenes from various crew and passengers throughout the Titanic's infamous voyage. It really eliminates the human ego— the class structures at play on the ship and the hubris that contributed to its sinking. With actors like Bonnie Milligan, Chuck Cooper and Ramin Karimloo, just to name a few, this cast is stellar — the ways they lean into the humor, the irony, and the tragedy so authentically really makes this production pop. There was one moment in particular with Chip Zien and Judy Kuhn which just broke me (if you know you know). And if you don't know, get yourself to City Center tomorrow July 23rd before Titanic closes. With that, another program for my collection.
